chunks: And when the Prophet confided a narration to one of his wives, and she disclosed it and God made it known to him, he made known part of it to her and concealed part of it. When he informed her about it, she asked: 'Who told you this?' He said: 'The All-Knowing, the All-Informed told me.'
ai.seo_question: Who did the Prophet say informed him of the secret his wife disclosed?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (66:3) is pivotal for discussing the Prophet's *'ismah* (infallibility) and the nature of his private disclosures, particularly regarding the permissibility of sharing secrets with spouses. The incident highlights the divine confirmation of his prophetic status, as he attributes the revelation not to human intelligence but to Allah, the All-Knowing. This event also serves as a legal basis for the prohibition of revealing confidential matters to one's spouse, emphasizing the sanctity of marital trust.
